P2500.title: Generator Lamp/L-Terminal Circuit Low
P2500.description: The L-terminal feedback line from the alternator (charging warning lamp circuit) reads below the lower limit. The lamp may stay on, and battery voltage may drift if regulation feedback is also affected.

causes.label: L-terminal shorted to ground
Alternator regulator failed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2501.title: Generator Lamp/L-Terminal Circuit High
P2501.description: The L-terminal feedback from the alternator reads above the upper limit — short to supply or open ground side. Charging diagnostics cannot run cleanly.

causes.label: L-terminal shorted to supply
Alternator regulator failed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2502.title: Charging System Voltage
P2502.description: The ECU detects an out-of-range charging system voltage without specifying high or low. Indicates a generic charging fault that requires further sub-code investigation.

causes.label: Alternator output fault
Voltage regulator fault

P2503.title: Charging System Voltage Low
P2503.description: The ECU detects that battery voltage during operation stays below the regulated target. The alternator output is insufficient to maintain charge under load, eventually leading to battery depletion.

causes.label: Weak alternator output
Faulty voltage regulator
Slipping drive belt

P2504.title: Charging System Voltage High
P2504.description: The ECU detects a battery voltage above the regulated upper limit. The voltage regulator is not limiting alternator output, risking damage to electronic modules and battery overcharge.

causes.label: Faulty voltage regulator
Poor alternator ground

P2505.title: ECM/PCM Power Input Signal
P2505.description: The ECM/PCM monitors the main switched battery feed (typically terminal 15 / ignition-switched supply via the main relay). A general fault is reported — either the input is missing entirely or it does not match the expected timing relative to ignition state. Engine may not start or stay running.

causes.label: Failed main relay
Blown fuse on the ECM power feed
Corroded connector pin at the ECM

P2506.title: ECM/PCM Power Input Signal Range/Performance
P2506.description: The switched-battery input to the ECM/PCM is present, but the level or transient behaviour is out of plausibility — sagging during cranking, slow ramp-up after main-relay close, or noisy. Often caused by aged main relay contacts or a weak battery feed under load.

causes.label: Aged main relay contacts with rising contact resistance
Weak battery sagging during crank
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2507.title: ECM/PCM Power Input Signal Low
P2507.description: The ECM/PCM switched-battery input reads below threshold while the ignition is on. Either the main relay does not close, the supply wire is broken or shorted to ground, or the battery is too low. Engine usually fails to start until the input recovers.

causes.label: Main relay does not pull in
Open supply wire
Severely discharged battery

P2508.title: ECM/PCM Power Input Signal High
P2508.description: The ECM/PCM switched-battery input reads above the upper threshold. Most often caused by a charging system overvoltage (failed alternator regulator) or wrong jump-start procedure. Sustained high voltage risks damaging ECU electronics.

causes.label: Alternator regulator overvoltage
Improper external power source or jump-start

P2509.title: ECM/PCM Power Input Signal Intermittent
P2509.description: The ECU detects sporadic interruptions of its supply voltage. The fault is set when supply drops below a threshold for short periods, often during cranking or due to a poor connection.

causes.label: Poor battery cable connection
Intermittent main relay
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P250A.title: Engine Oil Level Sensor Circuit
P250A.description: General electrical fault on the engine oil level sensor circuit. The ECM cannot read a plausible level signal (analog level, ultrasonic or capacitive sender). Without a valid level reading the ECM disables oil-low warnings and dynamic service-interval calculation.

causes.label: Open or shorted wiring to the sensor
Corroded connector at the oil pan

P250B.title: Engine Oil Level Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P250B.description: The oil level sensor is electrically intact, but the level reading is implausible — for example a constant value across drives, jumps that cannot match real oil consumption, or readings outside the design range. Often a contaminated or aged float/ultrasonic sender.

causes.label: Aged or contaminated sender
Foaming oil under high RPM masking the level
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P250C.title: Engine Oil Level Sensor Circuit Low
P250C.description: The oil level sensor signal voltage reads below the lower limit, typically a short to ground or an open at the reference end of the sender. The ECM treats the input as invalid and ignores oil-low warnings until the circuit is repaired.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to ground
Sender shorted internally
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P250D.title: Engine Oil Level Sensor Circuit High
P250D.description: The oil level sensor signal voltage reads above the upper limit, typically a short to reference voltage or an open signal return. Pegged at maximum, the ECM cannot distinguish full from invalid and disables the level monitor.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Open signal return
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P250E.title: Engine Oil Level Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P250E.description: The oil level signal jumps or drops out intermittently — usually loose contacts, vibration cracks at the sender or oil sloshing on bumpy roads. The ECM filters short transients but flags the input when the noise pattern exceeds the diagnostic limits.

causes.label: Loose or oil-soaked connector
Cracked sender housing
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P250F.title: Engine Oil Level Too Low
P250F.description: The oil level monitor reports the engine oil level below the safe minimum after sensor checks pass. Continued operation risks bearing damage and oil-pump cavitation, so the ECM sets a critical warning, may reduce torque and asks the driver to add oil immediately.

causes.label: High oil consumption between services
External oil leak
Missed top-up since last service

P2510.title: ECM/PCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Range/Performance
P2510.description: The voltage reported on the main power relay sense line for the engine controller does not match expectation. The ECU may shut down too early or stay awake too long, draining the battery.

causes.label: Main relay contacts pitted
Sense wiring corroded
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2511.title: ECM/PCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Intermittent
P2511.description: The sense (feedback) line that lets the ECM verify the main power relay has actually closed shows intermittent dropouts. The ECM expects to see battery voltage on this line whenever the relay is energised — short losses suggest aged contacts, vibration or chafed wiring.

causes.label: Aged main relay contacts
Chafed sense wire shorting intermittently
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2512.title: Event Data Recorder Request Circuit/Open
P2512.description: The Event Data Recorder (EDR / black box) request line — used by the ECM or restraint module to trigger the EDR to capture pre-crash data — is open. The ECM cannot trigger an event capture, so any subsequent crash event would not be recorded reliably.

causes.label: Open request wire or unplugged module
Failed input stage in the EDR
Pin pushed back out of connector body

P2513.title: Event Data Recorder Request Circuit Low
P2513.description: The EDR request line reads stuck low — typically a short to ground or a permanently asserted request. The ECM either sees a constant request (which it cannot service) or cannot pulse the line high to fire a real event capture.

causes.label: Request wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P2514.title: Event Data Recorder Request Circuit High
P2514.description: The EDR request line reads stuck high — typically a short to battery voltage. The ECM cannot pulse the line back low to release the request, so the EDR may either ignore further requests or sit in a permanent triggered state.

causes.label: Request wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2515.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor B Circuit
P2515.description: General electrical fault in the second A/C refrigerant pressure sensor circuit. Sensor B usually monitors the low-side or compressor-suction pressure (in addition to high-side sensor A). The ECM cannot read a plausible value and disables variable compressor control to avoid evaporator freeze-up or overpressure.

causes.label: Open or shorted wiring to the sensor
Failed sensor element

P2516.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P2516.description: A/C refrigerant pressure sensor B is electrically intact, but its reading does not match the system model — for example pressures that do not fall when the compressor is off, do not change with ambient temperature, or contradict pressure sensor A. Often a refrigerant charge issue or a contaminated sensor.

causes.label: Low refrigerant charge
Contaminated or aged sensor diaphragm
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2517.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor B Circuit Low
P2517.description: A/C refrigerant pressure sensor B signal voltage reads below the lower limit. Either a short to ground in the signal wire, an open reference voltage at the sensor, or an internal short. The ECM ignores the reading and disables A/C closed-loop control until the circuit recovers.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to ground
Missing 5 V reference at the sensor
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2518.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor B Circuit High
P2518.description: A/C refrigerant pressure sensor B signal voltage reads above the upper limit. Typically a short to reference voltage in the signal line, an open signal return, or an overpressure event briefly pegging the sensor. ECM disables variable compressor control to protect the system.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Open signal return at the sensor
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2519.title: A/C Request A Circuit
P2519.description: General electrical fault on the A/C compressor request input A. This input tells the ECM that the HVAC controller wants the A/C compressor engaged. With the input invalid, the ECM cannot enable the compressor clutch — A/C does not cool, idle-up compensation is not applied.

causes.label: Open or shorted A/C request wire
HVAC module not transmitting the request

P251A.title: PTO Enable Switch Circuit/Open
P251A.description: The Power Take-Off (PTO) enable switch input to the ECM is open. PTO is used on trucks and work vehicles to drive auxiliary equipment from the engine — without a valid enable signal the ECM refuses to enter PTO operating mode, idle speed control changes do not apply.

causes.label: Open switch wire or unplugged switch
Failed PTO enable switch
Pin pushed back out of connector body

P251B.title: PTO Enable Switch Circuit Low
P251B.description: The PTO enable switch input reads stuck low — typically a short to ground or a permanently closed switch. The ECM either sees PTO enabled when the operator has not requested it, or cannot release the PTO mode after work.

causes.label: Switch wire shorted to ground
Switch stuck closed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P251C.title: PTO Enable Switch Circuit High
P251C.description: The PTO enable switch input reads stuck high — typically a short to battery voltage. The ECM cannot pull the input low, so the switch state is unreadable and PTO mode is locked out for safety.

causes.label: Switch wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P251D.title: PTO Engine Shutdown Circuit/Open
P251D.description: The PTO engine-shutdown command line is open. This safety input lets a connected work attachment (or operator switch) request an immediate engine shutdown — for example when an interlock is opened on a stationary aerial work platform. With the line broken, the safety shutdown cannot be commanded.

causes.label: Broken shutdown wire or unplugged work attachment
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P251E.title: PTO Engine Shutdown Circuit Low
P251E.description: The PTO engine-shutdown command line reads stuck low — usually a short to ground or a permanently asserted shutdown request. The ECM may treat this as an active shutdown command and refuse to start or keep the engine running while in PTO mode.

causes.label: Shutdown wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P251F.title: PTO Engine Shutdown Circuit High
P251F.description: The PTO engine-shutdown command line reads stuck high — typically a short to battery voltage. The ECM cannot pulse the line low to acknowledge a shutdown request, so the operator-side safety chain is effectively disabled.

causes.label: Shutdown wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2520.title: A/C Request A Circuit Low
P2520.description: The A/C compressor request input A reads stuck low — typically a short to ground or a permanently asserted request. The ECM either sees A/C demanded all the time (cannot release idle-up, raises fuel use) or cannot distinguish a real request from the stuck low level.

causes.label: Request wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P2521.title: A/C Request A Circuit High
P2521.description: The A/C request input A reads stuck high — typically a short to battery voltage. The ECM cannot pull the line low to read switch state, so the A/C compressor request is treated as invalid and the clutch stays disengaged.

causes.label: Request wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2522.title: A/C Request B Circuit
P2522.description: General electrical fault on the second A/C request input B. Many vehicles have two HVAC zones, a rear evaporator request, or a redundant request line — input B carries that signal. With the input invalid, the ECM cannot honour zone B compressor demand or rear-evap operation.

causes.label: Open or shorted A/C request wire B
HVAC module not transmitting request B

P2523.title: A/C Request B Circuit Low
P2523.description: The A/C request input B reads stuck low — short to ground or permanently asserted request. Same effect as input A stuck low, applied to the second HVAC channel.

causes.label: Request wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P2524.title: A/C Request B Circuit High
P2524.description: The A/C request input B reads stuck high — typically a short to battery voltage. The ECM cannot read the switch state, request B is treated as invalid.

causes.label: Request wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2525.title: Vacuum Reservoir Pressure Sensor Circuit
P2525.description: General electrical fault on the vacuum reservoir pressure sensor circuit. The reservoir stores manifold or pump-generated vacuum for systems like brake booster, EGR actuators or HVAC dampers. Without a valid reading the ECM disables vacuum-pump duty cycle control.

causes.label: Open or shorted wiring to the sensor
Failed sensor element

P2526.title: Vacuum Reservoir Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P2526.description: The vacuum reservoir pressure sensor is electrically intact, but the reading does not match the model — vacuum that does not build up after pump activation, does not bleed off when consumers draw, or stays at one value. Often a partly clogged hose, a leaking reservoir or an aged sensor.

causes.label: Leaking reservoir or vacuum line
Aged sensor with offset drift
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2527.title: Vacuum Reservoir Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
P2527.description: Sensor signal voltage below the lower limit — usually a short to ground or open reference. The ECM disables vacuum pump control until the input recovers.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to ground
Missing 5 V reference at the sensor
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2528.title: Vacuum Reservoir Pressure Sensor Circuit High
P2528.description: Sensor signal voltage above the upper limit — usually a short to reference voltage or open signal return. ECM disables vacuum pump control to avoid overshooting.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Open signal return
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2529.title: Vacuum Reservoir Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P2529.description: The sensor signal jumps or drops out intermittently — loose connector, vibration, or chafed harness. The ECM filters short transients but flags the input when noise exceeds limits.

causes.label: Loose connector
Chafed harness
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P252A.title: Engine Oil Quality Sensor Circuit
P252A.description: General electrical fault on the engine oil quality sensor — typically a capacitive/dielectric sensor that estimates oil aging from permittivity, viscosity proxies and conductivity. With no valid reading the dynamic service-interval algorithm falls back to the fixed-interval default.

causes.label: Open or shorted wiring to the sensor
Failed sensor electrode after long use

P252B.title: Engine Oil Quality Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P252B.description: The oil quality sensor is electrically intact, but the readings do not match the model — for example permittivity that does not change after an oil change, or shifts inconsistent with km/h driven. Often a contaminated electrode or oil that does not fit the sensor calibration.

causes.label: Contaminated sensor electrode
Oil grade outside the sensor calibration range
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P252C.title: Engine Oil Quality Sensor Circuit Low
P252C.description: Sensor signal voltage below the lower limit — typically a short to ground in the signal line or an internal short across the sensor electrode.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P252D.title: Engine Oil Quality Sensor Circuit High
P252D.description: Sensor signal voltage above the upper limit — typically a short to reference voltage or an open signal return.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P252E.title: Engine Oil Quality Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P252E.description: The oil quality sensor signal jumps or drops out — usually a loose connector at the oil pan, an oil-soaked harness or vibration cracks at the sensor housing.

causes.label: Loose oil-soaked connector
Cracked sensor housing
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P252F.title: Engine Oil Level Too High
P252F.description: The oil level monitor reports the engine oil level above the safe maximum after sensor checks pass. Overfilling raises foaming, blow-by and crankcase pressure — and on diesels with regen-by-injection, fuel dilution can drive the level up by itself. The ECM warns the driver and may flag for service.

causes.label: Overfilled at last service
Fuel dilution from incomplete DPF regeneration
Coolant intrusion (head gasket / cooler)

P2530.title: Ignition Switch Run Position Circuit
P2530.description: The ECU detects an electrical fault on the ignition switch run position input. The signal indicating that the ignition is in the run position is missing or implausible.

causes.label: Faulty ignition switch contacts
Wiring or connector fault

P2531.title: Ignition Switch Run Position Circuit Low
P2531.description: The ignition switch Run-position input reads stuck low — short to ground or a permanently closed contact. The ECM cannot tell when the operator releases the switch from Run, so accessory and crank logic gets confused.

causes.label: Run input wire shorted to ground
Switch contact stuck closed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2532.title: Ignition Switch Run Position Circuit High
P2532.description: The ignition switch Run-position input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open switch return. The ECM cannot detect when the operator turns the switch back to off/accessory, so module sleep and accessory power timeouts do not work correctly.

causes.label: Run input wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2533.title: Ignition Switch On/Start Position Circuit
P2533.description: General electrical fault on the ignition switch On/Start (terminal 50 / crank) input. The ECM uses this signal to know when the starter is energised — without it the ECM cannot raise fuel and timing for cranking, the engine struggles to start or stalls right after.

causes.label: Open or shorted On/Start wire

P2534.title: Ignition Switch On/Start Position Circuit Low
P2534.description: The On/Start input reads stuck low — short to ground or permanently closed contact. The ECM may see crank request when the key is at rest, blocking accessory functions or causing unexpected starter cut-off logic.

causes.label: On/Start wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P2535.title: Ignition Switch On/Start Position Circuit High
P2535.description: The On/Start input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage. The ECM cannot read the crank state, modules dependent on this signal are unable to time their wake-up correctly.

causes.label: On/Start wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2536.title: Ignition Switch Accessory Position Circuit
P2536.description: General electrical fault on the ignition switch accessory (terminal 75 / ACC) input. ACC tells the ECM that radio, fans, accessory loads should be powered without the engine running. With the input invalid, the body controller may misjudge accessory power timing.

causes.label: Open or shorted ACC wire

P2537.title: Ignition Switch Accessory Position Circuit Low
P2537.description: The ACC input reads stuck low — short to ground or permanently closed contact. The ECM may see ACC active continuously and refuse to enter sleep, draining the battery.

causes.label: ACC wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P2538.title: Ignition Switch Accessory Position Circuit High
P2538.description: The ACC input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage. The ECM cannot detect when the operator releases the switch from ACC, accessory power timeouts do not work.

causes.label: ACC wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2539.title: Low Pressure Fuel System Sensor Circuit
P2539.description: General electrical fault on the low-pressure fuel system sensor — typically the lift-pump or pre-supply pressure sensor that monitors the rail feeding the high-pressure pump. With no valid reading, the ECM cannot verify that lift pressure is sufficient for HP-pump intake.

causes.label: Open or shorted wiring to the sensor
Failed sensor element

P253A.title: PTO Sense Circuit/Open
P253A.description: The PTO sense (engagement feedback) line is open. This input tells the ECM whether the PTO clutch or driveline is actually engaged after a request — it closes the loop on the PTO enable command. With it broken, the ECM cannot confirm engagement and refuses to ramp up to PTO speed setpoints.

causes.label: Open sense wire
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P253B.title: PTO Sense Circuit Range/Performance
P253B.description: The PTO sense circuit is electrically intact, but the engagement feedback does not match the command. The ECM requests engage and sees no engaged feedback (or vice versa) within the expected time window — drive-line slip, sticky clutch, or a mis-adjusted limit switch.

causes.label: Sticky or worn PTO clutch
Mis-adjusted limit switch
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P253C.title: PTO Sense Circuit Low
P253C.description: The PTO sense input reads stuck low — short to ground or limit switch stuck closed. The ECM may see PTO continuously engaged.

causes.label: Sense wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P253D.title: PTO Sense Circuit High
P253D.description: The PTO sense input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open switch return. The ECM cannot detect engagement.

causes.label: Sense wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P253E.title: PTO Sense Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P253E.description: The PTO sense signal jumps or drops out — usually loose connectors, a chattering limit switch, or vibration on the work attachment.

causes.label: Loose connector
Chattering limit switch
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P253F.title: Engine Oil Deteriorated
P253F.description: The oil quality monitor concludes that the engine oil has reached the end of its useful life — based on permittivity, soot content, fuel dilution and total operating hours. The ECM requests an oil change before the next regen cycle to prevent accelerated bearing wear.

causes.label: Service interval exceeded
High DPF regeneration load with fuel dilution

P2540.title: Low Pressure Fuel System Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P2540.description: P2540 is the plausibility check of the low-pressure fuel sensor, which measures supply pressure between the in-tank or lift pump and the high-pressure pump. The signal is electrically valid but does not match the commanded or expected pressure. VW's 2014 Touareg book sets it on the 3.6 L V6 when the measured pressure deviates from target beyond calibrated limits. Ram's bulletin 18-021-25 for the 2025 Ram 3500 with the 6.7 L Cummins lists P2540 and P2543 among the faults addressed by a PCM software update, so calibration can play a role as well. A weak supply pump or a clogged filter produces a genuine deviation. P2539 is the circuit fault, P2541/P2542 low/high, P2543 intermittent. Expect hesitation or hard starting.

causes.label: Weak in-tank or lift pump causing real pressure deviation
Restricted fuel filter or kinked supply line
Low-pressure sensor reading offset
Outdated engine software (manufacturer update available)

symptoms: Hesitation or power loss under load

P2541.title: Low Pressure Fuel System Sensor Circuit Low
P2541.description: P2541 means the signal of the low-pressure fuel sensor is below its valid range - typically a short to ground on the signal line or a lost 5 V sensor supply. VW's 2014 specification books set it below 0.2 V on the Passat, CC and Touareg (VW wording: short to ground or low input), whereas a signal above 4.8 V leads to P2539. CARB requires every emissions-relevant input to be checked for circuit faults and out-of-range values. Without a valid reading the engine computer can only run the fuel supply pump on a substitute value, so pressure control becomes coarse. P2540 is the plausibility fault, P2542 the high-side fault, P2543 an intermittent signal. Symptoms range from none to hesitation under load or hard starting.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to ground
5 V reference supply missing or pulled down by another sensor
Failed low-pressure fuel sensor

P2542.title: Low Pressure Fuel System Sensor Circuit High
P2542.description: The low-pressure fuel system sensor signal voltage is above the upper limit. Either a short to reference voltage in the signal line, an open signal return, or a sensor reading pegged high after an internal failure. The HP-pump pressure-control strategy falls back to default.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Open signal return
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2543.title: Low Pressure Fuel System Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P2543.description: P2543 flags a low-pressure fuel sensor signal that drops out or jumps for short moments while staying inside its electrical range most of the time - a loose pin, a chafed wire or a sensor with an internal contact problem. Ram's bulletin 18-021-25 for the 2025 Ram 3500 with the 6.7 L Cummins lists P2543-00 next to P2540-00 among the faults corrected by a PCM software update, which shows that calibration can also produce entries. Other manufacturers do not publish thresholds for this code. CARB requires input components to be checked for circuit faults and, where feasible, rationality. P2541/P2542 describe a steady low or high signal, P2540 a plausibility fault. The code often comes and goes, sometimes with brief stumbling.

causes.label: Loose or corroded pin at the sensor connector
Chafed signal or supply wire with intermittent contact
Outdated engine software (manufacturer update available)

P2544.title: Torque Management Request Input Signal A
P2544.description: The ECU detects an invalid torque-management request signal A from another control unit (e.g. transmission, ESP, ABS) on the CAN bus. Cooperative torque control cannot be performed as expected.

causes.label: CAN communication error
Fault in requesting module

P2545.title: Torque Management Request Input Signal A Range/Performance
P2545.description: The ECM receives torque-management requests from other modules (TCM during shifts, ABS/ESC during traction events, hybrid controller). Input A is electrically intact but its values do not match the system model — out-of-range steps, jumps, or persistent values that other modules cannot confirm.

causes.label: Requesting module sending invalid values
Communication bus corruption between modules
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2546.title: Torque Management Request Input Signal A Low
P2546.description: Torque management input A reads stuck low — analog short to ground or message stuck at minimum value. The ECM cannot trust the request and falls back to a safe default.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to ground
CAN message stuck at minimum value

P2547.title: Torque Management Request Input Signal A High
P2547.description: Torque management input A reads stuck high — analog short to reference voltage or message stuck at maximum value. The ECM rejects the request to avoid running unintended high-torque commands.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
CAN message stuck at maximum value

P2548.title: Torque Management Request Input Signal B
P2548.description: General electrical fault on the second torque-management request input B. Used when more than one module needs to request torque adjustments — typically TCM on input A and ABS/ESC on input B, or chassis vs powertrain. With B invalid, only the A-side request is honoured.

causes.label: Open or shorted wire / invalid CAN message

P2549.title: Torque Management Request Input Signal B Range/Performance
P2549.description: Input B is electrically intact but the values are implausible — same failure mode as the A-side performance fault, applied to the second torque-management channel.

causes.label: Requesting module sending invalid values
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping

P254A.title: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 1 Circuit/Open
P254A.description: The PTO speed-selector switch 1 input is open. This switch lets the operator pick a preset PTO operating speed (idle, 800, 1200 rpm, etc.). With the input broken, the ECM cannot apply any operator-selected speed and falls back to a default speed.

causes.label: Open wire or unplugged switch
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P254B.title: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 1 Range/Performance
P254B.description: The selector input is electrically intact but the value is implausible — multiple positions asserted at once, or a value that cannot map to any of the configured speed presets. Often a sticky multi-position switch or a contaminated rotary contact.

causes.label: Contaminated rotary contact
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping

P254C.title: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 1 Circuit Low
P254C.description: PTO speed selector 1 input reads stuck low — short to ground or analog signal pegged at minimum. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.label: Switch wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P254D.title: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 1 Circuit High
P254D.description: PTO speed selector 1 input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or analog signal pegged at maximum.

causes.label: Switch wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P254E.title: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 1 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P254E.description: The PTO speed selector signal jumps or drops out — usually a worn rotary contact or vibration on the work attachment.

causes.label: Worn rotary contact
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
Harness routed against vibrating component

P254F.title: Engine Hood Switch Circuit
P254F.description: General electrical fault on the engine hood (bonnet) switch circuit. The hood switch tells the body controller and (on hybrids) the high-voltage system that the hood is open — used for security, alarm and HV-safety interlock. With the input invalid, alarm logic and HV interlock fall back to a safe state.

causes.label: Open or shorted hood-switch wire
Aged switch with corroded contacts

P2550.title: Torque Management Request Input Signal B Low
P2550.description: Torque management input B reads stuck low — short to ground or message at minimum. ECM rejects the request, only A-side is used.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to ground

P2551.title: Torque Management Request Input Signal B High
P2551.description: Torque management input B reads stuck high — short to reference voltage or message at maximum. ECM rejects the request to avoid unintended high-torque commands.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage

P2552.title: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit A Circuit
P2552.description: General electrical fault on the throttle/fuel inhibit input A. This input lets external safety functions (immobilizer, hybrid HV interlock, anti-theft) override the throttle or cut fuel delivery. With the input invalid the safety override is unreliable, so the ECM falls back to its safe default — typically inhibit asserted to err on the side of safety.

causes.label: Open or shorted inhibit wire

P2553.title: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit A Circuit Range/Performance
P2553.description: The throttle/fuel inhibit A signal is electrically intact but its value does not match the system context — for example asserted while the immobilizer reports OK, or de-asserted while a hybrid HV interlock is active. The ECM cannot trust the signal.

causes.label: Requesting module sending an inconsistent value
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping

P2554.title: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit A Circuit Low
P2554.description: Throttle/fuel inhibit A reads stuck low — short to ground or permanently asserted. ECM may treat it as continuous inhibit and refuse normal operation.

causes.label: Inhibit wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P2555.title: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit A Circuit High
P2555.description: Throttle/fuel inhibit A reads stuck high — short to battery voltage. ECM cannot read the inhibit state and falls back to the safe default.

causes.label: Inhibit wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2556.title: Engine Coolant Level Sensor/Switch Circuit
P2556.description: General electrical fault on the engine coolant level sensor/switch circuit. Many vehicles use a simple float-switch in the expansion tank, others use a continuous-level analog sensor. With the input invalid the ECM cannot warn for low coolant before overheating starts.

causes.label: Open or shorted wiring to the sensor
Corroded connector at the expansion tank

P2557.title: Engine Coolant Level Sensor/Switch Circuit Range/Performance
P2557.description: The coolant level sensor is electrically intact, but the readings are implausible — for example a level that does not move at all over many drive cycles, or jumps that cannot match real coolant loss. Often a stuck float, contaminated electrode or air-locked sensor.

causes.label: Stuck float
Trapped air around the sensor
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2558.title: Engine Coolant Level Sensor/Switch Circuit Low
P2558.description: Coolant level sensor signal voltage below the lower limit — short to ground or internal short. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P2559.title: Engine Coolant Level Sensor/Switch Circuit High
P2559.description: Coolant level sensor signal voltage above the upper limit — short to reference voltage or open signal return.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P255A.title: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 2 Circuit/Open
P255A.description: The second PTO speed-selector switch input is open. Switch 2 typically encodes a binary or multi-bit code together with switch 1 — together they select one of several preset PTO speeds. With switch 2 broken, only the half of the bit pattern is available, so several presets cannot be reached.

causes.label: Open wire or unplugged switch
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P255B.title: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 2 Range/Performance
P255B.description: PTO speed selector switch 2 is electrically intact but its value does not match a valid bit pattern — multiple positions asserted, or values that do not map to any preset.

causes.label: Contaminated rotary contact
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping

P255C.title: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 2 Circuit Low
P255C.description: PTO speed selector 2 input reads stuck low — short to ground or analog signal pegged at minimum. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.label: Switch wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P255D.title: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 2 Circuit High
P255D.description: PTO speed selector 2 input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or analog signal pegged at maximum.

causes.label: Switch wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P255E.title: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 2 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P255E.description: PTO speed selector 2 signal jumps or drops out — usually a worn rotary contact or vibration on the work attachment.

causes.label: Worn rotary contact
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
Harness routed against vibrating component

P255F.title: A/C Request A Circuit Range/Performance
P255F.description: The A/C request input A is electrically intact, but its value does not match the system context — for example asserted while the HVAC controller reports off, toggling rapidly, or sustained while compressor pressures cannot support it. The ECM disables A/C clutch engagement until the input becomes plausible.

causes.label: HVAC module sending inconsistent request
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping

P2560.title: Engine Coolant Level Low
P2560.description: The coolant level monitor reports the engine coolant below the safe minimum after sensor checks pass. Continued operation risks overheating, head warping and head-gasket failure. The driver is warned and the ECM may reduce engine power until the level is restored.

causes.label: External coolant leak (hose, radiator, water pump)
Missed top-up since last service
Head gasket leaking coolant into combustion

P2561.title: A/C Control Module Requested MIL Illumination
P2561.description: The A/C / HVAC control module has requested the ECM to illuminate the malfunction indicator (MIL) because of an emissions-relevant fault on its side. The original fault is stored in the HVAC module — this code only signals that the ECM has honoured the request.

causes.label: Internal fault in the HVAC module — read its DTCs

P2562.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor A Circuit
P2562.description: General electrical fault on the turbocharger boost control position sensor A — the feedback sensor on the wastegate or VGT actuator (often a contactless Hall sensor). Without valid position feedback the ECM cannot close the loop on boost control and falls back to open-loop duty cycle.

causes.label: Open or shorted wiring to the position sensor
Failed Hall element after thermal cycling

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P2563.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P2563.description: P2563 means the position feedback of the turbocharger boost control actuator - variable vanes or wastegate - does not match the commanded position, although the sensor circuit itself is electrically intact. GM's 2009 Duramax diesel table sets it when vane position differs from target by 15 % or more for 5 s (Type B, warning light after two trips). VW's 2014 Passat TDI book compares the control deviation with a map based on engine speed and torque, and VW bulletin 21-15-06 links P2563 on 2.0 L TDI engines to kinked vacuum hoses, a leaking vacuum diaphragm or a broken adjustment stud on the turbocharger. P2562/P2564/P2565 are circuit faults, P2566 an intermittent signal. Boost is often limited, so power drops noticeably.

causes.label: Kinked, twisted or leaking vacuum hose to the boost actuator
Leaking actuator diaphragm or sticking vanes
Broken or missing adjustment stud, actuator travel out of tolerance

symptoms: Noticeable loss of power, limp mode
Underboost code P0299 stored at the same time

P2564.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor A Circuit Low
P2564.description: Position sensor A signal voltage below the lower limit — short to ground in the signal line or open reference voltage at the sensor.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to ground
Missing 5 V reference at the sensor
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P2565.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor A Circuit High
P2565.description: Position sensor A signal voltage above the upper limit — short to reference voltage in the signal line or open signal return.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Open signal return
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P2566.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P2566.description: P2566 reports that the signal from the boost control position sensor flickers or drops out briefly instead of being steadily wrong. VW bulletins 21-15-04 (2015) and 21-15-06 (2020) for 2009-2014 Jetta, Golf and Jetta SportWagen with the 2.0 L TDI (CBEA, CJAA) list P2566 together with P2562-P2565 and P0299 for the complaint of lacking power; there the position sensor G581 sits in the vacuum diaphragm, and the repair path starts with vacuum hoses, diaphragm and the actuator travel. No thresholds are published. CARB requires turbocharger electronic components to be monitored as comprehensive components. P2563 is the plausibility fault, P2564/P2565 a steady low or high signal. Expect intermittent power loss and a warning light.

causes.label: Loose or corroded pin at the position sensor connector
Heat-damaged or chafed sensor wiring near the turbocharger
Worn position sensor in the actuator

symptoms: Intermittent loss of power or limp mode
Check engine light, sometimes going out again

P2567.title: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Temperature Sensor Circuit
P2567.description: P2567 is the general circuit fault of the sensor on a direct ozone reduction (DOR) radiator - a radiator with a catalytic coating that converts ground-level ozone in the passing air and earns low-emission vehicles an NMOG credit. CARB section (e)(14) requires the OBD system to detect a missing or deteriorated DOR function. No manufacturer publicly documents P2567 itself. VW's 2014 books (CC, Tiguan) use the sibling codes P2568-P2570 for radiator sensor G611, which reports an ID and temperature over LIN, and MINI fits a comparable sensor on the radiator of B46M PZEV engines to confirm the coated radiator. P2568 is the plausibility fault, P2569-P2571 low, high and intermittent. Often the radiator with its bonded sensor is replaced.

causes.label: Failed radiator identification/temperature sensor
Damaged sensor wiring or connector at the radiator
Replacement radiator without coating or without sensor fitted

symptoms: No change in driveability or engine cooling
Possible failed emissions inspection because of the stored code

P2568.title: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P2568.description: P2568 is the plausibility check of the sensor on a direct ozone reduction (DOR) radiator, whose coating converts ozone in the cooling air. VW's 2014 specification books for the CC and Tiguan set it on a failed ID check or a failed functional check of the temperature sensor. VW Tech Tip 19-12-01 explains that on 2009-2015 Eos, Jetta, GTI, Passat and Tiguan with the 2.0 L TSI (CCTA, CBFA) this code refers to the radiator identification sensor G611; a new radiator comes with the sensor packed separately, to be bonded on. A non-coated aftermarket radiator or an unbonded sensor therefore triggers P2568. P2569/P2570 are LIN electrical faults, P2567 the general circuit fault. CARB section (e)(14) requires DOR monitoring.

causes.label: Aftermarket radiator without ozone coating or without the identification sensor
Identification sensor not bonded after radiator replacement
Identification/temperature sensor failed its self-test

symptoms: Check engine light, often after a radiator replacement
No change in driveability or engine cooling

P2569.title: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
P2569.description: Direct Ozone Reduction (DOR) catalysts are coated radiator surfaces or dedicated catalysts that decompose tropospheric ozone passing over the radiator — used for low-emissions vehicles. The temperature sensor monitoring the DOR brick reads stuck low — short to ground or sensor short.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to ground
Sensor shorted internally
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P256A.title: Engine Idle Speed Selector Sensor/Switch Circuit/Open
P256A.description: The idle-speed selector input is open. On commercial vehicles this switch lets the operator pick a fast-idle setpoint (for example to keep auxiliary loads supplied). With the input broken, the ECM cannot apply an operator-selected idle speed.

causes.label: Open wire or unplugged switch
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptoms: Idle speed too high, too low, or unstable
Possible stalling at idle or after cold start

P256B.title: Engine Idle Speed Selector Sensor/Switch Range/Performance
P256B.description: The idle-speed selector input is electrically intact but the value does not match a valid preset — multiple positions or a non-mappable value. Often a sticky multi-position switch.

causes.label: Contaminated rotary contact
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping

symptoms: Idle speed too high, too low, or unstable
Possible stalling at idle or after cold start

P256C.title: Engine Idle Speed Selector Sensor/Switch Circuit Low
P256C.description: Idle-speed selector input reads stuck low — short to ground or analog signal at minimum. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.label: Switch wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

symptoms: Idle speed too high, too low, or unstable
Possible stalling at idle or after cold start

P256D.title: Engine Idle Speed Selector Sensor/Switch Circuit High
P256D.description: Idle-speed selector input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or analog signal at maximum. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.label: Switch wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Idle speed too high, too low, or unstable
Possible stalling at idle or after cold start

P256E.title: Engine Idle Speed Selector Sensor/Switch Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P256E.description: The idle-speed selector signal jumps or drops out — usually a worn rotary contact or vibration. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.label: Worn rotary contact
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
Harness routed against vibrating component

symptoms: Idle speed too high, too low, or unstable
Possible stalling at idle or after cold start

P256F.title: A/C Request B Circuit Range/Performance
P256F.description: A/C request input B is electrically intact but its value does not match the system context — same failure mode as the input A performance fault, applied to the second HVAC channel.

causes.label: HVAC module sending inconsistent request B
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping

P2570.title: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Temperature Sensor Circuit High
P2570.description: The DOR catalyst temperature sensor reads stuck high — short to reference voltage or open signal return. Without a valid temperature the ECM cannot enable the DOR efficiency monitor.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Open signal return
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P2571.title: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P2571.description: The DOR catalyst temperature sensor signal jumps or drops out — typically loose connectors or chafed wiring near the radiator pack.

causes.label: Loose connector
Chafed harness
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P2572.title: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Deterioration Sensor Circuit
P2572.description: General electrical fault on the DOR catalyst deterioration sensor circuit. This sensor estimates the remaining ozone-conversion capacity of the DOR coating — coating worn off the radiator surface, contaminated by salt or grime, or thermally aged. Without a valid signal the deterioration monitor is disabled.

causes.label: Open or shorted wiring

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P2573.title: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Deterioration Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P2573.description: The DOR deterioration sensor is electrically intact but its readings drift or do not match the model — for example a deterioration value that does not move with km/h driven, or moves implausibly fast.

causes.label: Aged sensor with offset drift
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P2574.title: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Deterioration Sensor Circuit Low
P2574.description: The DOR deterioration sensor signal voltage reads below the lower limit — short to ground or internal short.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P2575.title: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Deterioration Sensor Circuit High
P2575.description: The DOR deterioration sensor signal voltage reads above the upper limit — short to reference voltage or open signal return.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P2576.title: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Deterioration Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P2576.description: The DOR deterioration sensor signal jumps or drops out — typically loose connectors or chafed wiring near the radiator.

causes.label: Loose connector
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
Harness routed against vibrating component

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P2577.title: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold
P2577.description: The DOR catalyst no longer reduces tropospheric ozone with the required efficiency, based on the deterioration sensor and operating-time model. Coating worn off the radiator surface, contaminated by road salt and grime, or thermally aged after many heat cycles. Replacing the affected radiator/coating restores function.

causes.label: DOR coating worn off the radiator
Coating contaminated by salt and grime

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P2578.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Speed Sensor A Circuit
P2578.description: General electrical fault on the turbocharger/supercharger shaft speed sensor A — a high-frequency Hall or eddy-current sensor on the compressor shaft. The ECM uses turbo speed for overspeed protection (typically 200,000+ rpm) and for closed-loop boost on VGT systems. With no valid speed the ECM limits boost.

causes.label: Open or shorted wiring
Aged sensor with reduced output amplitude

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P2579.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Speed Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P2579.description: Turbo speed sensor A is electrically intact, but the speed reading does not match the model — for example a speed that does not climb when boost rises, drifts away from the air-mass-flow estimate, or jumps. Often blade-fouling, a contaminated sensor tip or aged element.

causes.label: Oil-contaminated sensor tip
Aged Hall element
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P257A.title: Vacuum Reservoir Control Circuit/Open
P257A.description: The control circuit that drives the vacuum reservoir control valve (or vacuum pump motor) is open. The ECM cannot energise the actuator, so vacuum is no longer maintained on demand and consumers like brake booster, EGR or HVAC dampers may run out of vacuum.

causes.label: Open control wire
Failed driver in the control module
Pin pushed back out of connector body

P257B.title: Vacuum Reservoir Control Circuit Low
P257B.description: The vacuum reservoir control circuit reads stuck low — short to ground or low-side driver stuck on. The actuator may be energised continuously when it should be off.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P257C.title: Vacuum Reservoir Control Circuit High
P257C.description: The vacuum reservoir control circuit reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open coil. The driver cannot pull the line low to actuate the valve/motor.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Open coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P257D.title: Engine Hood Switch Circuit Range/Performance
P257D.description: The hood switch is electrically intact, but its state is implausible — for example reporting hood-open while vehicle speed is rising, or rapid toggles. Usually a worn switch with high contact bounce or a misaligned hood actuator.

causes.label: Worn switch with contact bounce
Misaligned hood actuator
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P257E.title: Engine Hood Switch Circuit Low
P257E.description: The hood switch input reads stuck low — short to ground or stuck-closed switch. The body controller may treat the hood as permanently open and refuse to arm the alarm or close the HV interlock.

causes.label: Switch wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P257F.title: Engine Hood Switch Circuit High
P257F.description: The hood switch input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open switch return. The body controller cannot detect when the hood is opened.

causes.label: Switch wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2580.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Speed Sensor A Circuit Low
P2580.description: Turbo speed sensor A signal voltage below the lower limit — short to ground in the signal line or open supply.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to ground
Open supply at the sensor
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P2581.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Speed Sensor A Circuit High
P2581.description: Turbo speed sensor A signal voltage above the upper limit — short to reference voltage or open signal return.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P2582.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Speed Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P2582.description: Turbo speed sensor A signal jumps or drops out — vibration, oil mist on the sensor tip, or chafed wiring near the hot turbo.

causes.label: Oil mist on the sensor tip
Chafed harness near the turbo
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P2583.title: Cruise Control Front Distance Range Sensor Single Sensor or Center
P2583.description: General fault on the radar/lidar/camera distance-range sensor used by adaptive cruise control. On systems with a single sensor or three sensors with a center unit, this code refers to the central sensor — without it, ACC distance control is disabled and the system falls back to plain cruise.

causes.label: Dirty sensor surface (radar emblem / camera lens)
Sensor misaligned after a frontal impact
Failed sensor module

P2584.title: Fuel Additive Control Module Requested MIL Illumination
P2584.description: The fuel additive control module — typical for diesel cars with a separate Eolys/Cerine additive tank that aids DPF regeneration — has requested the ECM to illuminate the MIL because of an emissions-relevant fault on its side. The original fault is in the additive module itself.

causes.label: Internal fault in the fuel additive module — read its DTCs

P2585.title: Fuel Additive Control Module Warning Lamp Request
P2585.description: The fuel additive control module asks for the additive-low warning lamp to be illuminated — the additive tank (Eolys/Cerine, used to lower DPF regen temperature) is approaching empty or has reached a service threshold. Continued driving without refilling will eventually disable DPF regeneration.

causes.label: Additive tank low — service refill required

P2586.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor B Circuit
P2586.description: General electrical fault on the turbocharger boost control position sensor B — second position sensor on the same actuator (redundant Hall) or on a second turbo (twin-turbo, sequential or two-stage). With B invalid the ECM cannot cross-check actuator A and falls back to limited boost control.

causes.label: Open or shorted wiring to the position sensor
Failed Hall element

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P2587.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P2587.description: Position sensor B is electrically intact, but the reading does not track sensor A or the actuator-command model. Often a misaligned redundant sensor or aged element on a second turbo.

causes.label: Sensor mounting misaligned after service
Aged Hall element
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P2588.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor B Circuit Low
P2588.description: Position sensor B signal voltage below the lower limit — short to ground or open reference. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P2589.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor B Circuit High
P2589.description: Position sensor B signal voltage above the upper limit — short to reference voltage or open signal return.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P258A.title: Vacuum Pump Control Circuit A/Open
P258A.description: The control circuit driving the electric vacuum pump (used to maintain brake-booster vacuum on direct-injection or hybrid powertrains where the engine is not always running) is open. The ECM cannot run the pump on demand — booster vacuum drops, pedal feel hardens, brake assist may be reduced.

causes.label: Open control wire to the pump
Failed driver in the control module

P258B.title: Vacuum Pump Control Circuit A Range/Performance
P258B.description: The vacuum pump control circuit is electrically intact, but the pump response does not match the model — pump runs longer than expected to reach setpoint, current draw rises (mechanically tight) or vacuum does not build at all. Aged motor brushes, dry vanes or a leaking line are typical causes.

causes.label: Aged motor brushes or dry vanes
Leaking vacuum line
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P258C.title: Vacuum Pump Control Circuit A Low
P258C.description: The electric vacuum pump control circuit reads stuck low — short to ground or low-side driver stuck on. The pump may run continuously, drawing current and overheating, until the ECM disables the channel.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to ground

P258D.title: Vacuum Pump Control Circuit A High
P258D.description: The vacuum pump control circuit reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open coil/return. The driver cannot pull the line low to start the pump.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Open pump motor winding

P258E.title: PTO Enable Switch Performance
P258E.description: The PTO enable switch is electrically intact but its state does not match operating conditions — for example asserted while the vehicle is rolling above the PTO speed limit, or asserted/de-asserted in fast succession. The ECM rejects the request to avoid unsafe PTO engagement.

causes.label: Switch contact bounce
Switch operated while vehicle is moving

P258F.title: Torque Management Request Output Signal
P258F.description: The ECM/PCM produces a torque-management output signal for downstream consumers (TCM during shifts, hybrid module, transfer case) and detects a fault on this output — open, short, or feedback voltage outside expected range. Without it, downstream modules cannot synchronise their behaviour with the engine.

causes.label: Open or shorted output line
Downstream consumer not loading the line

P2590.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P2590.description: Position sensor B signal jumps or drops out — vibration on the actuator, oil mist contamination or chafed wiring near the hot turbo.

causes.label: Vibration-induced chafing of the harness
Oil mist on the sensor
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P2591.title: Cruise Control Front Distance Range Sensor Left
P2591.description: General fault on the left-side front distance-range sensor used by adaptive cruise. Multi-sensor radar arrays use left/center/right sensors for wider field-of-view and lane discrimination — without left, ACC may degrade to single-target tracking.

causes.label: Dirty sensor surface
Sensor misaligned after a frontal impact

P2592.title: Cruise Control Front Distance Range Sensor Right
P2592.description: General fault on the right-side front distance-range sensor used by adaptive cruise. Same role as the left sensor but covering the right field-of-view.

causes.label: Dirty sensor surface
Sensor misaligned after a frontal impact

P2593.title: Turbocharger Speed Sensor B Circuit
P2593.description: General electrical fault on the second turbocharger speed sensor B — used on twin-turbo, sequential or two-stage installations to read the second compressor shaft speed. Same role as sensor A on the second turbo.

causes.label: Open or shorted wiring

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P2594.title: Turbocharger Speed Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P2594.description: Turbo speed sensor B is electrically intact, but the speed reading does not match the boost or air-mass model — same failure mode as sensor A performance fault, applied to the second turbo.

causes.label: Oil-contaminated sensor tip
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P2595.title: Turbocharger Speed Sensor B Circuit Low
P2595.description: Turbo speed sensor B signal voltage below the lower limit — short to ground or open supply. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P2596.title: Turbocharger Speed Sensor B Circuit High
P2596.description: Turbo speed sensor B signal voltage above the upper limit — short to reference voltage or open signal return.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P2597.title: Turbocharger Speed Sensor B Circuit Intermittent
P2597.description: Turbo speed sensor B signal jumps or drops out — vibration, oil mist or chafed wiring at the second turbo.

causes.label: Oil mist on the sensor tip
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
Harness routed against vibrating component

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P2598.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor A Performance - Stuck Low
P2598.description: Position sensor A reports a value stuck near the low end of its travel even when the actuator is commanded to move. Either the actuator is mechanically stuck closed (wastegate jammed shut, VGT vanes seized at minimum opening) or the sensor itself is pegged low. Boost is uncontrolled — overboost on diesels with VGT, underboost on wastegate-stuck systems.

causes.label: Actuator mechanically stuck near low end
Sensor pegged low

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P2599.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor A Performance - Stuck High
P2599.description: Position sensor A reports a value stuck near the high end of its travel — actuator stuck open (wastegate held wide open, VGT vanes seized at maximum opening) or sensor pegged high. Boost suffers — typically underboost on VGT, overboost-protection-off on wastegate.

causes.label: Actuator mechanically stuck near high end

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P259A.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor B Performance - Stuck Low
P259A.description: Same condition as the A-side stuck-low fault, but on the second sensor / second turbo. Position sensor B reads stuck near the low end while the actuator is commanded.

causes.label: Actuator mechanically stuck near low end

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P259B.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor B Performance - Stuck High
P259B.description: Same as the A-side stuck-high fault, applied to sensor B / turbo B. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.

causes.label: Actuator mechanically stuck near high end

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P259C.title: Excessive Time To Enter Closed Loop Turbocharger A Boost Control
P259C.description: After start-up the boost-control loop on turbo A takes longer than the calibration limit to transition from open-loop to closed-loop control. Typically a slow-warming actuator (VGT vanes carbonised), a sluggish position sensor or a leaky pneumatic actuator that cannot follow setpoints quickly enough.

causes.label: Carbonised VGT vanes
Leaky pneumatic actuator

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P259D.title: Excessive Time To Enter Closed Loop Turbocharger B Boost Control
P259D.description: Same condition as the turbo A excessive-warm-up fault, applied to the second turbo. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.

causes.label: Carbonised VGT vanes

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P259E.title: Turbocharger A Boost Control Position At Low Limit
P259E.description: The boost-control actuator on turbo A has been operating at the low end of its travel for too long — the closed-loop controller is saturated against the lower stop trying to reach the boost setpoint. Indicates either a leak (wastegate held closed but boost still escapes) or commanded boost above what the engine can produce.

causes.label: Boost leak in the charge-air path
Failing turbocharger that cannot produce target boost

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P259F.title: Turbocharger A Boost Control Position At High Limit
P259F.description: The boost-control actuator on turbo A has been operating at the high end of its travel — the controller is saturated against the upper stop trying to bleed off boost. Indicates either a wastegate stuck closed, oversized turbo for the calibration, or commanded boost limits being exceeded by ambient conditions (cold dense air).

causes.label: Wastegate stuck closed

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P25A0.title: Turbocharger B Boost Control Position At Low Limit
P25A0.description: Turbocharger B Boost Control Position At Low Limit: the control module has detected this fault condition. This affects turbo/supercharger boost-pressure control.

causes.label: Boost leak in the charge-air path

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P25A1.title: Turbocharger B Boost Control Position At High Limit
P25A1.description: Turbocharger B Boost Control Position At High Limit: the control module has detected this fault condition. This affects turbo/supercharger boost-pressure control.

causes.label: Wastegate stuck closed

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P25A2.title: Brake System Control Module A Requested MIL Illumination
P25A2.description: The primary brake system control module (ABS/ESC/iBooster) has requested the ECM to illuminate the MIL because of an emissions-relevant fault on its side — for example a regenerative braking fault on a hybrid that affects driveline torque flow. The original fault is in the brake module.

causes.label: Internal fault in the brake module — read its DTCs

P25A3.title: Engine Hood Open
P25A3.description: After plausibility checks the body controller has concluded that the engine hood is genuinely open while the vehicle is operating. Used to suspend HV operation on hybrids/EVs (HV interlock), block remote engine start, and trigger the alarm if armed.

causes.label: Hood not properly latched
Failed hood latch sensor

P25A4.title: Fuel Mode Select Switch Circuit
P25A4.description: General electrical fault on the fuel mode select switch — used on bi-fuel vehicles (CNG/LPG/H2/gasoline) so the driver can pick the active fuel. With the input invalid, the ECM falls back to the default fuel and disables operator-selectable switching.

causes.label: Open or shorted switch wire

P25A5.title: Fuel Mode Select Switch Performance
P25A5.description: The fuel mode select switch is electrically intact, but its state does not match operating conditions — switched to gas while gas tank is empty, or fast toggling. The ECM rejects the request to avoid stalling.

causes.label: Switch contact bounce

P25A6.title: Fuel Mode Select Switch Circuit Low
P25A6.description: Fuel mode switch input reads stuck low — short to ground or stuck-closed contact. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.label: Switch wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P25A7.title: Fuel Mode Select Switch Circuit High
P25A7.description: Fuel mode switch input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.label: Switch wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P25A8.title: Fuel Mode Select Switch Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P25A8.description: Fuel mode switch signal jumps or drops out — worn contact or vibration. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.label: Worn switch contact
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
Harness routed against vibrating component

P25A9.title: Piston Cooling Oil Control Circuit/Open
P25A9.description: The piston-cooling oil-jet control circuit is open. Modern engines with under-piston oil jets switch them on under high load to cool the piston crown — controlled by a solenoid valve in the oil gallery. With the circuit broken, jets cannot be commanded on or stay locked off, raising piston temperatures under load.

causes.label: Open control wire to the solenoid
Open solenoid coil
Pin pushed back out of connector body

P25AA.title: Piston Cooling Oil Control Circuit Low
P25AA.description: The piston-cooling oil-jet control circuit reads stuck low — short to ground or low-side driver stuck on. The jets may be enabled continuously, raising oil pump load and lowering oil pressure to other consumers.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P25AB.title: Piston Cooling Oil Control Circuit High
P25AB.description: Control circuit stuck high — short to battery voltage or open coil/return. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P25AC.title: Piston Cooling Oil Control Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
P25AC.description: The control circuit is electrically intact, but the solenoid valve does not open when commanded — confirmed by oil-pressure or oil-temperature feedback that does not change after the activation pulse. Piston cooling does not engage under high load — risk of piston-crown overheating and ring-land cracks.

causes.label: Solenoid stuck closed by oil sludge
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P25AD.title: Piston Cooling Oil Control Circuit Stuck On
P25AD.description: The piston cooling solenoid does not close when commanded off — jets remain active when not needed. Oil pressure to top-end consumers may sag, and warm-up takes longer because the cooling jets remove heat from the pistons during cold start.

causes.label: Solenoid stuck open
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P25AE.title: Piston Cooling Oil Pressure Too Low
P25AE.description: With the piston-cooling jets commanded on, the dedicated oil-pressure sensor in that gallery reads below the safe threshold. Insufficient flow to the jets means real piston cooling is not happening — the ECM warns the driver and may reduce torque to protect the pistons.

causes.label: Low engine oil level
Sludge-clogged oil gallery
Worn oil pump

P25AF.title: Coolant Temperature Control Module Requested MIL Illumination
