P25AF.description: A dedicated coolant-temperature control module (used on engines with electric coolant pumps and electronic thermostats to keep the cylinder head and block at independent setpoints) has requested the ECM to illuminate the MIL because of an emissions-relevant fault on its side. Original fault is in that module.

causes.label: Internal fault — read the module DTCs

P25B0.title: Fuel Level Sensor A Stuck
P25B0.description: Fuel level sensor A (typically the float in the main fuel tank section) reports a value that does not change over a long driving distance — the float is mechanically stuck against the tank wall, baffle or pump module. Without level changes the EVAP monitor cannot run and remaining-range estimates are wrong.

causes.label: Stuck float
Bent float arm catching the tank wall

P25B1.title: Fuel Level Sensor B Stuck
P25B1.description: Same condition as sensor A stuck, applied to the second fuel level sensor B. Saddle tanks (often AWD vehicles) and large trucks use two sensors — one per tank chamber — averaged for total level. A stuck B leaves only A and reduces accuracy.

causes.label: Stuck float

P25B2.title: Fuel Level Sensor A or B Stuck
P25B2.description: The ECM detects that one of the two level sensors is stuck but cannot identify which from the available signals — for example because the saddle-tank algorithm sees implausible delta only intermittently. Both sensors should be inspected.

causes.label: One stuck float — inspect both

P25B3.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate A Stuck Open
P25B3.description: Wastegate A is mechanically stuck open. Exhaust gas bypasses the turbine even at low load — turbo cannot reach target speed, boost is permanently low and the engine feels asthmatic. Common causes are seized linkage, broken return spring or carbon-locked wastegate flap.

causes.label: Seized wastegate linkage
Broken return spring
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25B4.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate A Stuck Closed
P25B4.description: Wastegate A is mechanically stuck closed. The turbo cannot bleed off exhaust at high load — boost overshoots the setpoint, risking overboost cut-off and damage to the turbo bearing. Carbon-locked flap, seized linkage or aged actuator are typical causes.

causes.label: Carbon-locked wastegate flap
Seized linkage
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25B5.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate B Stuck Open
P25B5.description: Same as wastegate A stuck open, applied to the second wastegate (twin-turbo, sequential or two-stage). Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.

causes.label: Seized wastegate linkage
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25B6.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate B Stuck Closed
P25B6.description: Same as wastegate A stuck closed, applied to the second wastegate. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.

causes.label: Carbon-locked wastegate flap
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25B7.title: Auxiliary Ignition Switch On/Start Position Circuit
P25B7.description: General electrical fault on the auxiliary ignition switch On/Start input. Used on commercial vehicles or upfit applications where a second ignition switch (in a sleeper cab, work platform or crew compartment) can crank the engine.

causes.label: Open or shorted wire

P25B8.title: Auxiliary Ignition Switch On/Start Position Circuit Low
P25B8.description: Auxiliary ignition switch On/Start input reads stuck low — short to ground or stuck-closed contact. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.label: Wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P25B9.title: Auxiliary Ignition Switch On/Start Position Circuit High
P25B9.description: Auxiliary ignition switch On/Start input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.label: Wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P25BA.title: Regeneration Control Switch Circuit/Open
P25BA.description: The DPF/SCR forced-regeneration request switch — used on commercial vehicles to let the operator force a parked regeneration when the automatic regen has been postponed too often — is open. The ECM cannot honour an operator request for forced regen.

causes.label: Open switch wire
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P25BB.title: Regeneration Control Switch Circuit Low
P25BB.description: Regeneration control switch input reads stuck low — short to ground or stuck-closed contact. The ECM may see a constant regen request which it cannot service while the vehicle is moving.

causes.label: Switch wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P25BC.title: Regeneration Control Switch Circuit High
P25BC.description: Regeneration control switch input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.label: Switch wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P25BD.title: Unmetered Fuel - Forced Engine Shutdown
P25BD.description: The engine controller commanded a forced shutdown after detecting unmetered fuel reaching the combustion chambers. Common on diesels with leaking turbo seals or cracked intercoolers that drip oil into the intake — the engine then runs on the oil and can overspeed.

causes.label: Turbocharger oil seal leak feeds engine oil into the intake
Oil collected in the intercooler is sucked into the engine on load
Failed PCV / crankcase breather floods intake with oil mist

P25BE.title: Alternative Fuel Disable Control Circuit / Open
P25BE.description: The controller cannot drive the alternative-fuel disable line that switches a bi-fuel vehicle (CNG, LPG, hydrogen) back to gasoline. An open detected on the control side blocks the safety shutoff for the gas system.

causes.label: Broken wire or corroded connector on the disable control line
Open coil in the alt-fuel disable relay
Output driver in the alt-fuel control module faulty

P25BF.title: Alternative Fuel Disable Control Circuit High
P25BF.description: Voltage on the alternative-fuel disable control line is above the expected window. Often a short to battery upstream of the relay or a stuck-on driver in the control module.

causes.label: Disable control wire shorted to a B+ supply
Output driver stuck on inside the control module
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P25C0.title: Alternative Fuel Disable Control Circuit Low
P25C0.description: Voltage on the alternative-fuel disable control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a failed driver pulling the line low.

causes.label: Disable control wire shorted to ground
Low-side driver internally shorted
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P25C1.title: Alternative Fuel Disable Signal Circuit
P25C1.description: The feedback signal that confirms the alt-fuel disable command was carried out is missing or out of range. The fuel system cannot verify that the gas circuit is shut.

causes.label: Open feedback wire between relay and control module
Feedback contact in the disable relay corroded or stuck

P25C2.title: Alternative Fuel Disable Signal Circuit High
P25C2.description: The disable feedback signal sits above its valid window. Typical cause is a short to battery on the feedback wire or a failed pull-up in the input stage.

causes.label: Feedback wire shorted to a B+ supply
Pull-up resistor in the input stage failed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P25C3.title: Alternative Fuel Disable Signal Circuit Low
P25C3.description: The disable feedback signal sits below its valid window. Usually a short to ground or an open pull-up that lets the input float low.

causes.label: Feedback wire shorted to ground
Open pull-up resistor in the controller input
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P25C4.title: Brake Booster Temperature Sensor A Circuit
P25C4.description: The temperature sensor monitoring the electric brake booster (iBooster, eBooster) returns no usable signal. Without temperature feedback the controller derates booster assist to protect the motor.

causes.label: Open sensor element or broken sensor wire
Corroded connector on the booster sensor pigtail

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25C5.title: Brake Booster Temperature Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P25C5.description: The booster temperature sensor reading is implausible relative to commanded assist or coolant temperature. The signal moves too slowly, sticks, or never reaches expected values during operation.

causes.label: Sensor drift or contamination on the temperature element
Sensor not seated properly against the booster motor housing
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25C6.title: Brake Booster Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low
P25C6.description: The booster temperature signal is below the lower diagnostic threshold. Typical causes are a shorted sensor element or a short to ground in the harness.

causes.label: Internal short in the sensor element
Sensor signal wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25C7.title: Brake Booster Temperature Sensor A Circuit High
P25C7.description: The booster temperature signal is above the upper diagnostic threshold. Common causes are an open sensor or a short to a 5 V reference in the harness.

causes.label: Open sensor element
Sensor signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25C8.title: Brake Booster Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P25C8.description: The booster temperature signal jumps or drops out for short moments. Usually a loose connector or a chafed wire that opens during vibration or thermal expansion.

causes.label: Sensor connector not fully seated or pin tension lost
Harness chafed against booster housing or pedal bracket
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25C9.title: Brake System Control Module B Requested MIL Illumination
P25C9.description: A second brake system control module (typically the redundant secondary unit on by-wire or AV-grade brake systems) has signalled an emissions-relevant fault and requested the engine controller to switch on the MIL.

causes.label: Active DTC stored in the secondary brake module
Communication loss interpreted as MIL request

P25CA.title: Intake Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit / Open Bank 1
P25CA.description: The controller cannot drive the park-lock pin that secures the intake camshaft phaser on bank 1 in its base position at engine off. Without the lock, the next start can suffer poor combustion or rough idle until the phaser builds oil pressure.

causes.label: Open coil in the park-lock solenoid
Broken control wire between ECU and solenoid

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25CB.title: Intake Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit Low Bank 1
P25CB.description: The intake camshaft park-lock control line on bank 1 is below the expected voltage window. Usually a short to ground or a low-side driver shorted internally.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to ground
ECU low-side driver internally shorted
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25CC.title: Intake Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit High Bank 1
P25CC.description: The intake camshaft park-lock control line on bank 1 is above the expected voltage window. Typical causes are a short to battery or a stuck-on driver in the controller.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
ECU output driver stuck on
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25CD.title: Intake Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit / Open Bank 2
P25CD.description: The controller cannot drive the park-lock pin that secures the intake camshaft phaser on bank 2 in its base position at engine off. Without the lock, the next start can suffer poor combustion or rough idle until the phaser builds oil pressure.

causes.label: Open coil in the park-lock solenoid
Broken control wire between ECU and solenoid

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25CE.title: Intake Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit Low Bank 2
P25CE.description: The intake camshaft park-lock control line on bank 2 is below the expected voltage window. Usually a short to ground or a low-side driver shorted internally.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to ground
ECU low-side driver internally shorted
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25CF.title: Intake Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit High Bank 2
P25CF.description: The intake camshaft park-lock control line on bank 2 is above the expected voltage window. Typical causes are a short to battery or a stuck-on driver in the controller.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
ECU output driver stuck on
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25D0.title: Exhaust Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit / Open Bank 1
P25D0.description: The controller cannot drive the park-lock pin that secures the exhaust camshaft phaser on bank 1 in its base position at engine off. Without the lock, the next start can suffer poor combustion or rough idle until the phaser builds oil pressure.

causes.label: Open coil in the park-lock solenoid
Broken control wire between ECU and solenoid

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25D1.title: Exhaust Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit Low Bank 1
P25D1.description: The exhaust camshaft park-lock control line on bank 1 is below the expected voltage window. Usually a short to ground or a low-side driver shorted internally.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to ground
ECU low-side driver internally shorted
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25D2.title: Exhaust Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit High Bank 1
P25D2.description: The exhaust camshaft park-lock control line on bank 1 is above the expected voltage window. Typical causes are a short to battery or a stuck-on driver in the controller.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
ECU output driver stuck on
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25D3.title: Exhaust Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit / Open Bank 2
P25D3.description: The controller cannot drive the park-lock pin that secures the exhaust camshaft phaser on bank 2 in its base position at engine off. Without the lock, the next start can suffer poor combustion or rough idle until the phaser builds oil pressure.

causes.label: Open coil in the park-lock solenoid
Broken control wire between ECU and solenoid

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25D4.title: Exhaust Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit Low Bank 2
P25D4.description: The exhaust camshaft park-lock control line on bank 2 is below the expected voltage window. Usually a short to ground or a low-side driver shorted internally.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to ground
ECU low-side driver internally shorted
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25D5.title: Exhaust Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit High Bank 2
P25D5.description: The exhaust camshaft park-lock control line on bank 2 is above the expected voltage window. Typical causes are a short to battery or a stuck-on driver in the controller.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
ECU output driver stuck on
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25D6.title: Exhaust Heat Exchanger Exhaust Bypass Valve A Position Sensor Stop Performance
P25D6.description: During self-calibration of the exhaust heat exchanger bypass valve A, the position sensor never reached the expected mechanical stop. The controller cannot zero the position reference, so commanded openings will be inaccurate.

causes.label: Soot or carbon deposits prevent valve from reaching the stop
Worn linkage between actuator and valve flap
Position sensor not aligned with valve shaft

P25D7.title: Fuel Level Sensor C Circuit
P25D7.description: A third fuel level sensor (C) used on multi-tank trucks, dual-saddle SUVs, or auxiliary fuel systems returns no usable signal. Without it, calculated fuel level and EVAP monitor enabling will be off.

causes.label: Open sender resistor or broken float
Corroded tank pump module connector

P25D8.title: Fuel Level Sensor C Performance
P25D8.description: The third fuel level sensor reading does not change as expected with consumption or refuelling. Float may be sticking, or the resistor track has localised wear.

causes.label: Float arm stuck on baffle or fuel pump module
Worn spot on the resistor track at common fill level

P25D9.title: Fuel Level Sensor C Circuit Low
P25D9.description: The third fuel level sensor signal is below the lower diagnostic threshold. Usually a shorted sender or a short to ground in the harness.

causes.label: Internal short in the sender resistor
Signal wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P25DA.title: Fuel Level Sensor C Circuit High
P25DA.description: The third fuel level sensor signal is above the upper diagnostic threshold. Common causes are an open sender or a short to the 5 V reference.

causes.label: Open sender resistor
Signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P25DB.title: Fuel Level Sensor C Circuit Intermittent
P25DB.description: The third fuel level sensor signal jumps or drops out for short moments. Usually a loose connector or a chafed wire that opens during driving vibration.

causes.label: Tank module connector not fully seated
Harness chafed near tank straps
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P25DC.title: Fuel Level Sensor C Stuck
P25DC.description: The third fuel level sensor reads a constant value across known consumption or refuelling events. Float arm or resistor wiper is mechanically stuck.

causes.label: Float arm jammed against tank wall, baffle or pump module
Resistor wiper seized by varnish from old fuel

P25DD.title: A Camshaft Position - Stuck In Locked Position Bank 1
P25DD.description: Camshaft phaser A on bank 1 will not unlock from its base position. The phaser stays at the park-lock angle and cannot be advanced or retarded as commanded.

causes.label: Park-lock pin stuck in the locked groove
Low oil pressure cannot push the lock pin out
Oil control valve blocked by debris

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25DE.title: A Camshaft Position - Unable to Achieve Locked Position Bank 1
P25DE.description: Camshaft phaser A on bank 1 cannot reach its base position at engine shutdown so the lock pin never engages. Next cold start may run rough until oil pressure builds.

causes.label: Worn vanes or housing inside the phaser
Sludge or contaminated oil prevents return to base
Oil control valve leaks internally

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25DF.title: A Camshaft Position Control Performance Bank 1
P25DF.description: Camshaft phaser A on bank 1 follows the commanded angle too slowly, oscillates, or shows steady-state error outside tolerance. Closed-loop control of cam timing is degraded.

causes.label: Oil control valve spool sticks under varnish
Stretched timing chain shifts cam reference
Wrong oil viscosity slows phaser response

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25E0.title: A Camshaft Position - Stuck In Locked Position Bank 2
P25E0.description: Camshaft phaser A on bank 2 will not unlock from its base position. The phaser stays at the park-lock angle and cannot be advanced or retarded as commanded.

causes.label: Park-lock pin stuck in the locked groove
Low oil pressure cannot push the lock pin out
Oil control valve blocked by debris

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25E1.title: A Camshaft Position - Unable to Achieve Locked Position Bank 2
P25E1.description: Camshaft phaser A on bank 2 cannot reach its base position at engine shutdown so the lock pin never engages. Next cold start may run rough until oil pressure builds.

causes.label: Worn vanes or housing inside the phaser
Sludge or contaminated oil prevents return to base
Oil control valve leaks internally

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25E2.title: A Camshaft Position Control Performance Bank 2
P25E2.description: Camshaft phaser A on bank 2 follows the commanded angle too slowly, oscillates, or shows steady-state error outside tolerance. Closed-loop control of cam timing is degraded.

causes.label: Oil control valve spool sticks under varnish
Stretched timing chain shifts cam reference
Wrong oil viscosity slows phaser response

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25E3.title: B Camshaft Position - Stuck In Locked Position Bank 1
P25E3.description: Camshaft phaser B on bank 1 will not unlock from its base position. The phaser stays at the park-lock angle and cannot be advanced or retarded as commanded.

causes.label: Park-lock pin stuck in the locked groove
Low oil pressure cannot push the lock pin out
Oil control valve blocked by debris

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25E4.title: B Camshaft Position - Unable to Achieve Locked Position Bank 1
P25E4.description: Camshaft phaser B on bank 1 cannot reach its base position at engine shutdown so the lock pin never engages. Next cold start may run rough until oil pressure builds.

causes.label: Worn vanes or housing inside the phaser
Sludge or contaminated oil prevents return to base
Oil control valve leaks internally

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25E5.title: B Camshaft Position Control Performance Bank 1
P25E5.description: Camshaft phaser B on bank 1 follows the commanded angle too slowly, oscillates, or shows steady-state error outside tolerance. Closed-loop control of cam timing is degraded.

causes.label: Oil control valve spool sticks under varnish
Stretched timing chain shifts cam reference
Wrong oil viscosity slows phaser response

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25E6.title: B Camshaft Position - Stuck In Locked Position Bank 2
P25E6.description: Camshaft phaser B on bank 2 will not unlock from its base position. The phaser stays at the park-lock angle and cannot be advanced or retarded as commanded.

causes.label: Park-lock pin stuck in the locked groove
Low oil pressure cannot push the lock pin out
Oil control valve blocked by debris

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25E7.title: B Camshaft Position - Unable to Achieve Locked Position Bank 2
P25E7.description: Camshaft phaser B on bank 2 cannot reach its base position at engine shutdown so the lock pin never engages. Next cold start may run rough until oil pressure builds.

causes.label: Worn vanes or housing inside the phaser
Sludge or contaminated oil prevents return to base
Oil control valve leaks internally

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25E8.title: B Camshaft Position Control Performance Bank 2
P25E8.description: Camshaft phaser B on bank 2 follows the commanded angle too slowly, oscillates, or shows steady-state error outside tolerance. Closed-loop control of cam timing is degraded.

causes.label: Oil control valve spool sticks under varnish
Stretched timing chain shifts cam reference
Wrong oil viscosity slows phaser response

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25E9.title: Supercharger Disconnect Clutch Stuck Open
P25E9.description: The clutch that engages the mechanical supercharger to the engine drive will not close. The supercharger stays disengaged so boost from this stage is unavailable, which limits torque and may also affect cooling pump drives shared with the same belt.

causes.label: Open electromagnetic clutch coil
Worn friction surfaces leave the air gap too large to attract
Corroded armature plate stuck open

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P25EA.title: Supercharger Disconnect Clutch Stuck Closed
P25EA.description: The clutch that engages the mechanical supercharger to the engine drive will not open. The supercharger remains coupled at all loads, increasing parasitic loss and fuel consumption when boost is not needed.

causes.label: Armature plate seized to the pulley face
Driver stuck on keeps clutch energised
Failed pulley bearing welds clutch surfaces

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P25EB.title: Supercharger Disconnect Clutch Circuit Range/Performance
P25EB.description: The supercharger clutch control current does not match the commanded value within tolerance. Either coil resistance has drifted or the driver feedback is implausible.

causes.label: Coil resistance increased due to thermal damage
High-resistance contact in the clutch connector
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P25EC.title: Supercharger Disconnect Clutch Circuit Low
P25EC.description: Voltage on the supercharger clutch control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted clutch coil.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in the clutch coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P25ED.title: Supercharger Disconnect Clutch Circuit High
P25ED.description: Voltage on the supercharger clutch control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open coil that lets the driver float high.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
Open clutch coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P25EE.title: Vacuum Pump Control Circuit B / Open
P25EE.description: The controller cannot drive the secondary electric vacuum pump (B). Brake servo or HVAC actuators that depend on engine vacuum may not get enough vacuum during low-load operation or with engine off in stop-start mode.

causes.label: Open pump motor winding or worn brushes
Broken control wire between ECU and pump

P25EF.title: Vacuum Pump Control Circuit B Range/Performance
P25EF.description: The secondary vacuum pump does not produce the expected vacuum within the commanded run time. Leak in the pump line or worn pump diaphragm reduces output.

causes.label: Worn diaphragm or vanes inside the pump
Cracked vacuum hose or loose connection
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P25F0.title: Vacuum Pump Control Circuit B Low
P25F0.description: Voltage on the secondary vacuum pump control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted motor winding.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in pump motor winding

P25F1.title: Vacuum Pump Control Circuit B High
P25F1.description: Voltage on the secondary vacuum pump control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open motor that lets the driver float high.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
Open motor winding or worn brushes

P25F2.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor C Circuit
P25F2.description: A third boost pressure sensor (C) used on twin-stage or sequential boost systems returns no usable signal. Without it, boost control of the third stage runs open-loop or is disabled.

causes.label: Open sensor element or broken signal wire
Corroded connector at sensor pigtail

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25F3.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor C Circuit Range/Performance
P25F3.description: The third boost pressure sensor reading is implausible compared with manifold pressure or commanded boost. Either drift, leak in the sensing line, or contamination on the sensor diaphragm.

causes.label: Sensor drift after thermal aging
Sensing hose blocked by oil residue
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25F4.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor C Circuit Low
P25F4.description: The third boost pressure sensor signal is below the lower diagnostic threshold. Usually a shorted sensor element or a short to ground.

causes.label: Internal short in the sensor element
Signal wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25F5.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor C Circuit High
P25F5.description: The third boost pressure sensor signal is above the upper diagnostic threshold. Common causes are an open sensor or a short to the 5 V reference.

causes.label: Open sensor element
Signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25F6.title: AIR System B
P25F6.description: A general fault in the second secondary air injection (AIR) circuit. Detected by the O2 sensors which expect a lean swing during cold-start AIR pump operation but do not see one.

causes.label: Failed AIR pump motor or impeller
Check valve seized by exhaust soot
Corroded or cracked air injection pipe

P25F7.title: AIR System B Incorrect Flow Detected
P25F7.description: The second AIR system delivers measurably more or less air than expected. Often a partially blocked pipe, a worn pump, or a leak between pump and check valve.

causes.label: Air pipe partially blocked by carbon
Worn pump impeller reduces flow
Leak between pump and check valve

P25F8.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve C Control Circuit
P25F8.description: A third bypass (recirculation or wastegate) valve used in three-stage charging systems is not responding to control commands. Boost balancing across stages can no longer be achieved.

causes.label: Open solenoid coil
Open or shorted wiring to the valve

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P25F9.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve C Control Circuit Low
P25F9.description: Voltage on the third bypass valve control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted solenoid coil.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in the solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P25FA.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve C Control Circuit High
P25FA.description: Voltage on the third bypass valve control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open solenoid coil.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
Open solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P25FB.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve C Control Circuit Range/Performance
P25FB.description: The third bypass valve current does not match the commanded value within tolerance. Drifted coil resistance or high-resistance contact in the connector.

causes.label: Coil resistance changed by thermal stress
High-resistance contact in the valve connector
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P25FC.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve C - Mechanical
P25FC.description: The third bypass valve is mechanically jammed. Solenoid is energised correctly but the valve flap or disc does not move as expected.

causes.label: Carbon buildup blocks the valve flap
Actuator linkage seized by corrosion

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25FD.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve C Temperature Too High
P25FD.description: The third bypass valve has reached over-temperature. Either coil duty cycle is too high for too long, or cooling air flow around the valve is restricted.

causes.label: Sustained high duty cycle from charge balancing strategy
Cooling air channel blocked by debris

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25FE.title: Supercharger Disconnect Clutch
P25FE.description: A general performance fault in the supercharger disconnect clutch. Engagement or release is slow, sticky, or out of tolerance without a clear electrical-side cause.

causes.label: Worn friction surfaces or air gap drift
Oil or debris on the clutch face

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P25FF.title: Electrical System Voltage Stabilizer Control Module Performance
P25FF.description: The voltage stabiliser module (DC/DC converter for stop-start engine cranking events) does not maintain the regulated 12 V output during high transient loads. Sensitive electronics may reset during cranking.

causes.label: Aged smoothing capacitors lose capacitance
Battery condition causes input voltage to drop too far
Internal fault in the converter switching stage
